guigang.type: Largest Inland Port in Western China
guigang.desc: The Guigang Port area is one of the largest inland river ports in China - a major hub where goods are transshipped between river barges and road transport. The riverfront has been developed into a scenic promenade with views of the busy port operations, cargo vessels, and the river. Fascinating for those interested in China logistics and river trade.

guigang.name: Guiping Xishan (桂平西山)
guigang.desc: Xishan (West Mountain) in Guiping City is one of Guangxi most famous scenic areas - a dramatic karst peak rising from the plains with a historic Buddhist temple at its base. The temple has been continuously operating for over 1,000 years. A cable car takes visitors to the summit for panoramic views of the karst landscape and surrounding countryside.

guigang.name: Taiping Uprising Memorial Hall
guigang.desc: The Guiping area was a key stronghold of the Taiping Uprising (1850-1864), the massive peasant rebellion led by Hong Xiuquan that nearly toppled the Qing Dynasty. The water is exceptionally clear (visibility 30+ meters) and the reefs support extraordinary marine biodiversity - coral gardens, tropical fish, sea turtles, and rays. Diving trips to the Xisha Islands depart from Sanya and Wenchang on Hainan Island.

sansha.name: North Reef (七连屿)
sansha.desc: North Reef (七连屿) is a string of seven coral islands and reefs north of Yongxing Island, known for its bird sanctuary. The islands are covered in sea birds and have pristine white sand beaches surrounded by turquoise lagoon water. Access is by boat from Yongxing Island. The reef is considered one of the most beautiful spots in the Paracel Islands.

sansha.name: Phoenix Island (琛航岛)
sansha.desc: Phoenix Island (琛航岛) hosts the Paracel Islands Martyrs Cemetery (西沙海战烈士陵园), commemorating the 1974 Xisha (Paracel) Islands battle between China and South Vietnam. The memorial honors the Chinese naval personnel who died in the conflict that secured Chinese control of the Paracel Islands. A place of significant historical and patriotic significance.

yueyang.name: Dongting Lake (洞庭湖)

The lake changes dramatically with the seasons - large and deep in summer, exposing vast reed beds and sandbanks in winter. Boat tours on the lake offer views of fishing communities, lotus fields, and migratory birds. The lake is most dramatic in summer when it is full to the brim.
